name: The Mommyheads
label: Simple Machines
lede: Adam Cohen's New York art-pop band went west, made a Beatles-schooled record for Geffen, vanished, and came back as one of indie's most prolific cult acts.

eras.title: Fame kids with four-tracks
eras.text: Adam Cohen and his high-school friends start a band in New York City, learning songwriting on cheap recording gear. The first records already hint at the ornate pop to come.

years.h: Adam Cohen starts The Mommyheads in New York
years.p: The band forms around 1987 as a New York project of Adam Cohen, with drummer [[Jan Kotik|4a251c11-a62e-4e29-a578-c745532b1799]] and bassist Matt Patrick among the early players. Members came out of the city's performing arts high school scene.

years.h: Magumbo Meatpie EP, cut with Wharton Tiers
years.p: The first record, on Sit & Spin, was recorded by Wharton Tiers, the engineer known for his work with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]].

years.h: Acorn on Fang Records
years.p: The debut album, produced by Chris Rael, pairs Adam Cohen with Jan Kotik and Matt Patrick. Fang was a small label, but the record kept circulating for years.

eras.title: West to San Francisco, Simple Machines
eras.text: Cohen becomes Adam Elk to avoid confusion with another Adam Cohen, moves the band west and meets the lo-fi network around Simple Machines. A new rhythm section arrives.

years.h: Adam Cohen becomes Adam Elk and the band moves to San Francisco
years.p: Wikipedia says he changed his name to avoid confusion with Leonard Cohen's musician son. Keyboardist Michael Holt and drummer Dan Fisherman join around this move, and Jan Kotik is out.
years.xp:
The move west, to San Francisco in 1990, changed the band's line-up as well as its zip code. Holt and Fisherman became the core partners for Elk that still anchor the band today.

Kotik would not be gone from the story: the band later reunited around a tribute show for him.

years.h: Swiss Army Knife: home demos on Simple Machines
years.p: The cassette collects Adam Elk's four-track demos and lands on Simple Machines, the Arlington, Virginia label run by [[Jenny Toomey|246fc8dd-a667-4a5b-868a-a5897bcd6c59]] and Kristin Thomson. Sources date it 1990 to 1992.

years.src: Glide Magazine · Stratton's Setlist · Wikipedia: Mommyheads
years.h: Coming Into Beauty: the first full-band record for Simple Machines
years.p: Recorded in New York at 6/8 Studios and in Chico, California at Cloud 9, with Elk, Holt, Fisherman and Matt Patrick. Elk and Patrick wrote most of the material.
years.xp: The album is the band's most experimental early work, and it sat out of print for decades. It was remastered by Fred Kavorkian at Avatar Studios and reissued digitally in February 2021 with new artwork by Marc Stromberg.

eras.title: Flying Suit, Bingham's Hole
eras.text: Jeff Palmer takes over on bass and the songs grow more lavish. Two independent albums make the band a name with people in the business.

years.h: Jeff Palmer replaces Matt Patrick on bass
years.p: Wikipedia dates Patrick's tenure as 1987–1993. Palmer arrives in time for Flying Suit.

years.h: Flying Suit on Dromedary Records
years.p: The first album with Jeff Palmer on bass arrives on Dromedary, a small independent.

years.h: Bingham's Hole, produced by Peter Katis
years.p: Released on Dot Dot Dash, the record is a big step up in polish and draws the ear of producer Don Was.
years.xp: Peter Katis produced the album, years before he became known for his work with bands like The National. Its reception led to a major-label deal.

eras.title: Geffen, briefly
eras.text: Producer Don Was champions the band, and a major label lets them make a big, Beatles-minded record. Then the label loses interest.

years.h: Don Was and Geffen: the self-titled album with Tower of Power horns
years.p: Was co-produced The Mommyheads with the band at Ocean Way, with Tower of Power's horns on "Wake Up Irene" and [[Jon Brion|a32e4aac-1db8-4dc6-be34-a813c4530627]] on Chamberlin keyboard for "Screwed" and "Thought of You."
years.xp:
The lead single was "Jaded," and the record earned a Bammie nomination. The New York Times' Jon Pareles wrote that the band was out to capture longing in "perfectly balanced melodies."

According to Wikipedia, the album was barely marketed by Geffen, and the band went dormant for over a decade soon after, even though they toured North America behind it.

years.h: Dropped by Geffen, the band plays a last San Francisco show
years.p: Wikipedia says the label dropped them during a restructuring, and the band ends after a final San Francisco show.

eras.title: A tribute show, and the band is back
eras.text: The death of the band's first drummer draws the old line-up together, and the reunion sticks.

years.h: Jan Kotik, the band's first drummer, dies of cancer
years.p: Wikipedia says Kotik died December 13, 2007 after a three-year battle with cancer, though AllMusic and other outlets date the reunion to 2008.

years.h: A tribute show for Jan Kotik turns into a reunion
years.p: Elk, Holt and Fisherman reunite (with Jeff Palmer on bass in 2008) to honor Kotik, and keep going. You're Not a Dream follows the same year.
years.xp: In the decade before, Elk had released the solo album Labello and worked as a composer for TV commercials. Palmer had joined Sub Pop's [[Sunny Day Real Estate|86b24e8f-a4d9-4c84-83ee-fde0d14ad9fa]], Holt made solo records, and Fisherman worked as a computer programmer and educator.

years.h: You're Not a Dream: the comeback record
years.p: The first new album since the Geffen days starts a remarkably prolific second act.

years.h: Finest Specimens and a Scandinavian fanbase
years.p: The retrospective on Dromedary collects unreleased tracks. AllMusic notes an unexpectedly passionate following in Scandinavia.

years.h: Jason McNair takes over on bass
years.p: McNair joins on bass and has stayed, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: Forty years and still writing
eras.text: The Mommyheads work at a steady clip, with concept albums, Swedish tours and college-radio wins.

years.h: Delicate Friction: first all-new material since the 1990s
years.p: Followed a year later by Vulnerable Boy.

years.h: The Geffen album is reissued, and Big Takeover calls it a masterpiece
years.p: The 1997 self-titled album is reissued, alongside the new New Kings of Pop.

years.h: Coming Into Beauty is remastered and reissued
years.p: Fred Kavorkian remasters the 1992 Simple Machines album, with new cover art by Marc Stromberg.

years.h: Age of Isolation reaches #29 on college radio
years.p: Wikipedia cites it as their highest college-radio ranking to that point.

years.h: Coney Island Kid: a concept album about 1970s Brooklyn
years.p: Elk toured Sweden and the US behind the record.

years.h: One Eyed Band hits #10 on college radio
years.p: Wikipedia calls it a career peak, and it makes year-end lists. No Quietus followed in November 2025.
